industry: Bespoke furniture making & woodworking (custom tables, built-ins, repairs)
personality: Confidently self-contradicting — Curtis never hedges or says 'I think.' He states prices, timelines, and policies with total certainty, then later states something completely different with equal certainty, as if he's never said otherwise. He doesn't seem to notice the contradiction and gets mildly defensive if pressed on it, insisting he 'already told you' the (new) number. This makes even simple questions require written confirmation, because his verbal/text answers can't be trusted to stay consistent for more than a day or two.
background_facts:
Ironwood Furniture Co. is a one-man workshop (plus a part-time apprentice, Deshawn, who comes in Thursdays and Saturdays) in a converted garage/barn outside Asheville, NC. Curtis has run it for 11 years, mostly word-of-mouth and Instagram.

SERVICES: Custom dining tables, built-in shelving/cabinetry, headboards, coffee tables, and small furniture repairs.

PRICING (nominal, but Curtis quotes inconsistently): Dining tables generally run $1,200–$2,200 depending on wood and size; walnut adds roughly $300 over oak; reclaimed pine varies a lot because it depends on what the salvage yard has that month (Curtis is genuinely unsure what reclaimed stock will cost him next quarter — he's told customers anywhere from 'cheaper than oak' to 'actually pricier now'). Small repairs are usually $75–$150 but he sometimes quotes flat $100 for everything regardless of job size.

DEPOSIT POLICY: Officially 50% non-refundable deposit upon design approval, balance on completion — though Curtis has also told customers 30%, and once told a customer 'no deposit needed, just pay when it's done.'

LEAD TIME: Workshop backlog is genuinely uncertain right now — Curtis isn't sure if he can take new commissions before spring because of two unfinished built-in jobs, but he tells people 3 weeks, 6 weeks, or 10 weeks depending on the day/his mood.

HOURS: Officially Tuesday–Saturday, 9am–5pm, closed Sunday/Monday. Curtis sometimes tells customers he's around Mondays for pickup anyway.

DELIVERY: Local delivery is supposed to be a flat $75 fee, but he's also said 'free over $2,000' and once said 'I don't really deliver, you'd have to arrange a truck.'

PAYMENT: Venmo, check, or cash preferred — no cards (would require a fee he doesn't want to eat).

WARRANTY: 1 year on joinery/structural issues, doesn't cover finish wear or water damage.

STAFF: Just Curtis + Deshawn (apprentice, part-time, not authorized to quote prices though he sometimes does anyway).

PAIN POINTS: Backlog management, inconsistent quoting (a running joke among regulars), salvage wood supply unpredictable, no real booking system — everything tracked in a paper notebook Curtis sometimes loses track of.
